greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. We gather today in the peace of Christ, seeking the light of His truth in the midst of our own journey.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the God of the living, have mercy on us.
Christ Jesus, you are our rock and our fortress, have mercy on us.
Lord Jesus, you call us to the glory of the resurrection, have mercy on us.
psalm_response: Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!
homily:
We often think of the temple as a place of stone and mortar, a fixed location where we go to find God. But today, on this feast of the Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, we are reminded of something far more intimate. We are reminded that Mary herself was the first living temple, the first human being to be set apart entirely for the indwelling of the Most High. She was a child, small and fragile in the eyes of the world, yet she carried a purpose that would eventually change the trajectory of all human history. She was a witness, a lampstand, as the Book of Revelation describes, standing before the Lord of the earth. 

I want you to hold onto this image: the lampstand. It is a vessel meant to hold light, meant to be placed where the darkness is deepest. Think of Benjamin Vo. Think of the way he carried his own light. Ben was a boy who loved the architecture of things—the way a Boeing 737 was constructed, the logic of a line of code, the systems that make the world move. He was a boy who looked at the world with a brilliant, searching mind, always seeking to understand how the pieces fit together. But more than that, he was a lampstand of kindness. He was the boy who, when he was just fifteen, felt the weight of his uncle William’s suffering and wanted to hand over his entire piggy bank—his entire security—to help. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it; the offering itself was the light. It was the pure, unadulterated desire to be a blessing to someone else. That is the light that does not go out. That is the lampstand that remains, even when the world seems to grow dark.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: five months have passed. The calendar page turns, but the heart often stays in the room where he last smiled. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the quick laugh, the bright smile, the way he would share his dreams of 'con chim airlines'—are suddenly met with an empty space. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ache when a memory ambushes you in the middle of an ordinary day. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer. Your tears are not a lack of faith; they are the language of love that has no place left to go.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame for the randomness of the world’s suffering. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. The Sadducees come to Jesus with a riddle, a cold, clinical question about marriage and resurrection. They want to trap him in the logic of this age. But Jesus looks past their cynicism. He points to the bush—the burning bush—and reminds them that God is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He says, 'He is not God of the dead, but of the living, for to him all are alive.' This is the hinge of the mystery. We often think that death is the end of the story, the final line in the code, the point where the system shuts down. But Jesus tells us that for God, there is no 'dead.' There is only the living. Benjamin is not a memory tucked away in a photo album; he is a living soul in the Banquet of Heaven. He is fully alive, fully healed, and fully embraced by the Father. He is standing in the light of the Resurrection, and in that light, he is more 'Ben' than he ever was here. He is the boy who loved to dream, the boy who giggled at the idea of his own airline, the boy who looked at the world with such profound curiosity. He is all of that, and he is with the God of the living.

Consider the two witnesses in the Book of Revelation: the olive trees and the lampstands. They finish their testimony, they face the beast, they seem to be conquered, but then, a breath of life from God enters them. They stand on their feet. They are called up to heaven. This is the promise of every baptized soul. Ben’s time on earth was a finished testimony of love. He gave everything he had—his brilliance, his kindness, his gentle heart. And now, the breath of life from God has raised him up. He has heard the voice from heaven say, 'Come up here.' And he has gone up in a cloud of glory. He is not lost. He is just ahead of you. He is waiting in the place where there is no more pain, no more struggle, only the fullness of life.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. The God of the living is the God who is with you right now in this very room, in the silence, in the ache, and in the hope that refuses to die. 

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of His face shine upon you as you walk in His peace. Go in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the light of Christ and the joy of the Resurrection.
For all who are grieving, especially Ben’s parents and his brother Ryan, that they may be consoled by the promise of the living God and find hope in His enduring love.

readings.label: Reading
readings.text:
I, John, heard a voice from heaven speak to me:
Here are my two witnesses:
These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands
that stand before the Lord of the earth.
If anyone wants to harm them, fire comes out of their mouths
and devours their enemies.
In this way, anyone wanting to harm them is sure to be slain.
They have the power to close up the sky
so that no rain can fall during the time of their prophesying.
They also have power to turn water into blood
and to afflict the earth with any plague as often as they wish.When they have finished their testimony,
the beast that comes up from the abyss
will wage war against them and conquer them and kill them.
Their corpses will lie in the main street of the great city,
which has the symbolic names “Sodom” and “Egypt,”
where indeed their Lord was crucified.
Those from every people, tribe, tongue, and nation
will gaze on their corpses for three and a half days,
and they will not allow their corpses to be buried.
The inhabitants of the earth will gloat over them
and be glad and exchange gifts
because these two prophets tormented the inhabitants of the earth.
But after the three and a half days,
a breath of life from God entered them.
When they stood on their feet, great fear fell on those who saw them.
Then they heard a loud voice from heaven say to them, “Come up here.”
So they went up to heaven in a cloud as their enemies looked on.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R.    (1b) Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!
Blessed be the LORD, my rock,
who trains my hands for battle, my fingers for war.
R.    Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!
My mercy and my fortress,
my stronghold, my deliverer,
My shield, in whom I trust,
who subdues my people under me.
R.    Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!
O God, I will sing a new song to you;
with a ten stringed lyre I will chant your praise,
You who give victory to kings,
and deliver David, your servant from the evil sword.
R.    Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Some Sadducees, those who deny that there is a resurrection,
came forward and put this question to Jesus, saying,
“Teacher, Moses wrote for us,
If someone’s brother dies leaving a wife but no child,
his brother must take the wife
and raise up descendants for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers;
the first married a woman but died childless.
Then the second and the third married her,
and likewise all the seven died childless.
Finally the woman also died.
Now at the resurrection whose wife will that woman be?
For all seven had been married to her.”
Jesus said to them,
“The children of this age marry and remarry;
but those who are deemed worthy to attain to the coming age
and to the resurrection of the dead
neither marry nor are given in marriage.
They can no longer die,
for they are like angels;
and they are the children of God
because they are the ones who will rise.
That the dead will rise
even Moses made known in the passage about the bush,
when he called  ‘Lord’
the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob;
and he is not God of the dead, but of the living,
for to him all are alive.”
Some of the scribes said in reply,
“Teacher, you have answered well.”
And they no longer dared to ask him anything.

pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.

pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
